en: When Mayon Volcano shows a level 3 alert, you must evacuate beyond the six-kilometer Extended Danger Zone.
When PAGASA raises Wind Signal Number 3, secure loose roofs because winds can exceed 100 kilometers per hour.
Living near the West Valley Fault requires securing heavy furniture to prevent injuries during a strong earthquake.
After wading in flooded Manila streets, wash your feet thoroughly to prevent leptospirosis caused by rat urine.
During summer, Metro Manila's heat index often exceeds 40 degrees Celsius, so drink water to prevent heat stroke.
Apply sunscreen before visiting Boracay Beach because strong tropical ultraviolet rays can cause severe sunburns and skin damage.
When climbing Mount Pulag, wear thick layers because the summit temperature can drop below freezing, causing dangerous hypothermia.
During the rainy season in Luzon, empty stagnant water around your house to prevent Aedes mosquitoes from spreading dengue.
When hiking in the Sierra Madre mountain range, stay on marked trails to avoid getting lost in dense forests.
Always boil water from rural deep wells for one minute to kill harmful bacteria before drinking it.
When swimming in Palawan, wear aqua shoes to protect your feet from sharp coral reefs and venomous stonefish.
During heavy monsoon rains, avoid crossing the Cagayan River because sudden flash floods can occur without warning.
